summary.scope: Likely: a scheduled check on Mission end dates, a configurable lead-time window, and a notification sent to one or more roles (freelancer's manager, client contact by role, possibly the freelancer) via email and/or in-app, with logic to avoid duplicate notifications when the mission date changes.
assumptions: The notification is about an existing Mission entity linked to a Freelancer and a Client (per platform context).

summary.blind_spot: The request names only the notification, but end-of-mission is a cascading event in this platform (final invoicing, validation, downstream automation). briefs.problem: Approaching mission end-dates aren't surfaced to anyone in time, so renewal, final invoicing, and offboarding steps happen late or get missed.
briefs.solution: An automated check on Mission end-dates that fires a notification to the relevant people ahead of the end date.
introduces: a scheduled/background job that scans Mission records for approaching end-dates
a recipient-routing rule engine (role- and/or client-specific) layered on the existing Client Contact model
state tracking to avoid duplicate or stale alerts when a mission's end date moves or the mission is cancelled
a new notification channel/config surface likely shared with other modules (Contract, Invoicing) that already route by contact role

challenges.headline: "The right people" is undefined
challenges.premise: The request assumes there's a known, fixed set of people to notify when a mission is ending.
challenges.alternative: In this platform, notification routing is typically role- and client-specific (billing/operational/HR contact, mission manager, staffing admin) and often varies by contract terms.
challenges.consequence: Hardcoding a single recipient (e.g. mission manager only) means the first client who wants their operational contact copied forces a rebuild of the routing logic.
challenges.recommendation: Define the recipient matrix (role × client × mission type) with the client before estimating, not during UAT.

challenges.headline: Single implicit trigger timing
challenges.premise: "About to end" is treated as one alert at one unstated lead time.
challenges.alternative: Different downstream actions (renewal decision, final invoicing, offboarding paperwork) usually need different lead times and often a staggered sequence (e.g. 30/15/7 days), not one fire-and-forget alert.
challenges.consequence: A single fixed-lead alert will be too early to be actionable for some teams and too late for others, and gives no defined behavior when the end date is extended, brought forward, or the mission is cancelled after the alert already fired.
challenges.recommendation: Map each downstream action to its own required lead time and define re-evaluation/cancellation logic before building the scheduler.

challenges.headline: Notification alone may not fix the problem
challenges.premise: The request frames this purely as 'send a notification', but the stated success metric is that renewal, final invoicing and offboarding actually happen on time.
challenges.alternative: A notification that isn't acted on still produces a late offboarding — some teams solve this with a lightweight tracked task/checklist per mission end, with an owner and a due date, not just an email.
challenges.consequence: Building notification-only risks meeting the letter of the request while missing the actual success criteria if alerts get lost in an inbox.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether they need alerting only, or a trackable end-of-mission checklist that surfaces overdue actions.

complexity_reasons: configurable per-client/per-role recipient routing rather than a single hardcoded recipient
scheduling logic that must tolerate date changes, cancellations and avoid duplicate sends
integration with the existing Client Contact role and permission model
undecided channel and sync-vs-async delivery adds design uncertainty
briefs.cost_driver: the configurable recipient-routing rule engine (role- and client-specific)
risks: The existing notification/permission framework may not yet support routing by contact role per client — likely needs extension, not reuse as-is.
Mission end dates can change after a reminder is scheduled; without idempotency handling this produces duplicate or missed alerts.
No current-process baseline is defined, making it hard to prove after launch that the feature actually reduced late actions.
Scope can silently grow from 'send a notification' into a full end-of-mission task-tracking workflow if success metrics aren't pinned down early.

opportunities.text: The Client Contact role-based routing built for this feature can become the shared notification-routing mechanism other modules already need (contract signature, invoice issuance).

The 'approaching deadline' scheduler pattern (scan a date, alert before it, handle date drift) mirrors contract renewal and amendment reminders and could be generalized into a reusable lifecycle-reminder engine.

next_steps: Define the recipient rule (who, by role, per client/contract) with actual stakeholders before scoping the build.
Pin down lead time(s), recurrence, and behavior when the end date changes or the mission is cancelled after a reminder is scheduled.
Clarify whether the client needs alert-only or a trackable checklist tied to renewal/invoicing/offboarding completion.
Confirm notification channel and whether delivery should be synchronous or a scheduled batch job.

challenges.headline: Single-fire vs. reminder cadence
challenges.premise: The request reads as one notification when the mission is 'about to end.'
challenges.alternative: Comparable systems in this platform (approval circuits, renewal alerts) typically use a cadence — e.g. reminders at 30/15/5 days — with escalation if no action is taken, since renewal or offboarding decisions take real time to execute.
challenges.consequence: A one-shot alert can arrive too late for the action it's meant to trigger, or get missed entirely, defeating the stated purpose of the feature.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether this is a single alert or a reminder sequence before building the scheduler.

challenges.headline: Hardcoded rule on a configurable platform
challenges.premise: Lead-time and recipients are described as if one global rule will cover every mission.
challenges.alternative: This is a multi-client configurable platform where equivalent rules (approval circuits, notification routing) already vary by client and contract; the lead-time and recipient set are likely to need the same treatment.
challenges.consequence: Hardcoding forces a rebuild the first time a client asks for a different threshold or recipient set — expensive rework given the rule and config slots are currently completely undefined.
challenges.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether lead-time/recipients are configurable per client before estimating the build.

challenges.headline: 'Right people' left undefined
challenges.premise: The request treats the recipient list as self-evident.
challenges.alternative: In this platform, notification routing is driven by a Contact's role (billing/operational/HR), not just 'the client' or a single internal owner — the same pattern should likely apply here.
challenges.consequence: Guessing recipients risks notifying the wrong contact or skipping the one who actually needs to act (e.g. the billing contact for final invoicing), silently defeating the feature.
challenges.recommendation: Map explicit recipient roles (internal mission owner, client contact by role, freelancer) with the client before implementation.

Hook end-of-mission into a generic downstream-automation trigger (invoicing, offboarding) rather than a bespoke chain specific to this feature.
